Q: Seemingly bad design choices in C++? Why are things the way they are? A:

Building blocks. One of the driving ideologies of the C++ Standard Library is to provide small, simple features that can easily be assembled into more complicated behaviour. This leads to decisions like thread not joining: Why add on an easily implemented feature that makes it hard to get the simpler behaviour when its needed? RAII Is the bee's knees most of the time, but if you force it on everything, you lose valid ways to express behaviour.

Is it really better for a program to hang on a join of a thread that'll never be ready to exit or crash out because you have a bug in the code? No one likes it when a program crashes, but at least you know you have a problem and can start the recovery process, be that immediately debugging the program or restarting the service and continuing as normal until a solution is found and the program is patched.

Q: Service: typeof is not assignable to type 'Provider[]' A:

The ApidataService has to be added as the second item in the providers list like this:

providers: [
        { provide: APP_BASE_HREF, useValue: 'http://localhost:4200/' },
        { provide: ApidataService, useClass: ApidataService }
     ],

or shorter:

providers: [
        { provide: APP_BASE_HREF, useValue: 'http://localhost:4200/' },
        ApidataService
     ],

Q: Identify if a column is Virtual in Snowflake without SHOW COLUMNS A:

INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS:

KIND The kind of column. Possible values:

  • COLUMN: A regular table column.
  • VIRTUAL_COLUMN: A computed column defined by an expression.
  • PARTITION_COLUMN: An external table partition column.

Identifying all virtual columns in a database:

USE DATABASE <db_name>;

SELECT *
FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS
WHERE KIND = 'VIRTUAL_COLUMN';

Related: ACCOUNT_USAGE.COLUMNS:

SELECT * 
FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.COLUMNS
WHERE DELETED IS NULL
  AND KIND = 'VIRTUAL_COLUMN';

Q: I used CentOS 9 to test CETAN server but I got the error below (in attached). Could you please show me what’s wrong and how to make it work? A:

The error: GLIBCXX_3.4.32 not found means your system is too old. In the document at https://www.cetan.io/quickstart.html, at the very end we already mentioned this error.

You have two options:

Option 1: Upgrade the existing CentOS

Run the commands below to upgrade:

sudo dnf update libstdc++ -y

sudo dnf groupinstall “Development Tools” -y

Option 2: Upgrade the VM to a newer Linux version (CentOS 10 or Ubuntu 13)

CentOS is redhat base, so the create user command is a bit different:

sudo useradd —system —no-create-home —user-group cetan

That’s it.

Disclosure: I work on CETAN.
